title: Energy shocks are widening the policy response from transition deployment to reserves, affordability, access, and supply-chain resilience
source_unit: International Energy Agency, State of Energy Policy 2026
geography: Global energy-policy landscape across 84 countries, with policy, affordability, access, regulatory, and supply-chain examples across regions

observations.period: 2025-2026; global policy inventory and crisis response

denominator.unit: IEA global energy-policy landscape reviewed through the Global Energy Policies Hub

policy_measures_tracked.unit: energy-policy measures tracked across the IEA inventory, more than

countries_covered.unit: countries covered by the policy inventory

dominant_policy_themes.value: cost of living, competitiveness, resilient supply chains, energy security, efficiency, and sustainability

observations.method: IEA synthesis of the Global Energy Policies Hub, policy changes, emergency responses, and longer-run energy-policy trends.
observations.uncertainty: A policy inventory establishes government action or announcement, not implementation quality, fiscal execution, public acceptance, energy-system performance, or household benefit.
observations.subgroup: Governments, energy firms, infrastructure providers, households, workers, consumers, importing states, and communities exposed to energy-price or supply disruptions.
observations.counterinterpretation: A broad policy response can reflect institutional learning and resilience, but it can also produce fragmented, costly, or contradictory measures across jurisdictions.

observations.period: 2022-2026; emergency reserves, demand restraint, and energy-system preparedness

denominator.unit: global oil and natural-gas emergency-preparedness policy frame

countries_with_oil_gas_emergency_measure.unit: countries with emergency measures for oil and natural-gas supply disruptions

oil_import_coverage.unit: percent of global oil imports accounted for by countries with stockholding and emergency-response legislation

gas_storage_requirement_countries.unit: countries that adopted gas-storage requirements or strategic buffers since 2022, close to

demand_restraint_measures.value: energy-conservation campaigns, work-from-home policies, and fuel rationing

observations.method: IEA comparison of emergency legislation, strategic stocks, gas buffers, and crisis-response measures across importing and exposed countries.
observations.uncertainty: Legal preparedness and stockholding coverage do not establish reserve adequacy, release speed, equitable access, or whether demand-restraint measures are sustained.
observations.subgroup: Energy-importing governments, utilities, firms, commuters, households, workers, and users of transport, heating, and electricity systems.
observations.counterinterpretation: Reserves and demand restraint can reduce disruption exposure, while maintaining them may impose fiscal, storage, or distributional costs and may not protect all places equally.

denominator.unit: government energy-affordability interventions and vehicle incentives reviewed by IEA

household_support_2022_2023.unit: US dollars disbursed to households through emergency energy-affordability support between 2022 and 2023, approximately

vulnerable_household_targeting.unit: percent of short-term interventions since 2022 targeted at vulnerable households most exposed to price shocks

targeted_vehicle_incentives_2025.unit: percent of 2025 incentives for efficient or alternative-fuel vehicles that were targeted, about

support_mechanism_shift.value: movement toward auctions and market-based support for solar and wind

observations.method: IEA review of emergency energy-affordability support, transport incentives, and renewable-support mechanisms.
observations.uncertainty: Spending and targeting shares do not measure take-up, adequacy, incidence, household energy burden, or whether market-based support lowers final consumer costs.
observations.subgroup: Low-income households, energy-intensive households and firms, vehicle buyers, renewable developers, taxpayers, and public-budget managers.
observations.counterinterpretation: Broad support may stabilize markets quickly, while targeted support can miss eligible households or impose administrative barriers; market-based schemes may lower fiscal exposure over time.

denominator.unit: global energy-efficiency, electrification, access, and supply-chain policy frame

renewable_nuclear_policy_countries.unit: countries with active policies to advance renewable and nuclear deployment as of April 2026

efficiency_electrification_policy_countr.unit: countries with energy-efficiency and electrification policies as of April 2026

supply_chain_resilience_policy_countries.unit: countries with policies incentivising supply-chain resilience and diversification across critical minerals and clean-energy technologies as of April 2026

energy_access_policy_activity.value: 56 electricity-access policies and 64 clean-cooking initiatives implemented or announced since the 2024 IEA Summit on Clean Cooking in Africa

efficiency_regulatory_balance.value: 30 percent of regulated energy consumption experienced a rollback compared with 17 percent subject to new, stricter rules in 2025

observations.method: IEA synthesis of deployment, efficiency, electrification, clean-cooking, energy-access, supply-chain, and regulatory-policy changes.
observations.uncertainty: Country policy counts and regulatory direction do not establish actual deployment, access, emissions, affordability, reliability, or durable implementation; aggregate counts can conceal reversals and uneven coverage.
observations.subgroup: Energy users, households without electricity or clean cooking, firms, workers, regulators, technology suppliers, importing states, and communities exposed to infrastructure decisions.
observations.counterinterpretation: Policy foundations may enable faster transition and access gains, while regulatory rollbacks, delayed standards, fiscal constraints, and supply-chain concentration can slow or unevenly distribute those gains.

related_sources.claim: Official IEA report landing page and citation metadata for State of Energy Policy 2026.
IEA overview dashboard for the policy inventory and report findings.

boundary: This record adds a policy-adoption and implementation route linking geopolitical shocks to reserves, demand restraint, affordability support, regulation, energy access, transition deployment, and supply-chain resilience. It is not respondent-level data, household survey evidence, proof of implementation quality, realized consumer benefit, or a forecast of emissions or energy-system outcomes.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: Official IEA State of Energy Policy 2026 executive summary and report landing page were reviewed; policy-inventory scope, emergency preparedness, affordability targeting, market-based support, energy access, regulatory changes, and April 2026 policy counts were cross-checked.
